st.1: Temple architecture is regarded as the hallmark of the Indus Valley Civilisation.

x: Neither statement is correct: town planning, not temple architecture, is the hallmark of the Indus Valley Civilisation; no clear remains of temples or palaces have been found in Harappan cities.

st.2: They were mostly of chert, spherical in shape and carried no markings.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the weights were binary in the lower and decimal in the higher denominations. They were mostly chert and cubical, not spherical; the unit weight was about 13.63 g, not 136.3 g.

st.1: The cylindrical steatite seal found at Rakhigarhi in June 2026 carries an alligator motif and five Harappan characters.

x: All three statements are correct: the Rakhigarhi seal (June 2026) shows an alligator and five characters; the unicorn is the commonest seal motif and the pipal the commonest tree.

st.1: The Satavahana inscriptions are in the Sanskrit language.
st.2: The Junagadh inscription of Skandagupta is the first long inscription in Sanskrit.

x: Neither statement is correct: Satavahana inscriptions are in Prakrit, not Sanskrit; the first long Sanskrit inscription is the Junagadh inscription of Rudradaman I, not Skandagupta's later record there.

st.1: The Harivamsa is appended to the Mahabharata.

x: All three statements are correct: the Harivamsa is an appendix of the Mahabharata; its core, the Jaya, had 8,800 shlokas; it has 18 parvas.

st.1: It is a Sanskrit drama of the Gupta age by Vishakhadatta.

x: All three statements are correct: the Mudrarakshasa is Vishakhadatta's Sanskrit play of the Gupta age, in which Chanakya wins over Rakshasa; Dhundiraja made Chandragupta a scion of the Nandas.

st.3: Dionysius was sent by Ptolemy II Philadelphus to the court of Bindusara.

x: All three statements are correct: Megasthenes came to Chandragupta Maurya; Deimachus (from Antiochus I) and Dionysius (from Ptolemy II) came to Bindusara.

st.2: James Prinsep identified Sandrocottus with Chandragupta Maurya in 1793.
st.1: Justin and Strabo call him Androkottus, while Arrian and Plutarch call him Sandrocottus.

x: None of the statements is correct: Justin and Strabo use Sandrocottus and Arrian and Plutarch Androkottus; the identification (1793) was made by Sir William Jones, not Prinsep; it is Justin, not Pliny, who describes the meeting with Alexander.

st.3: They contain Ashoka's account of the Kalinga war and its casualties.
st.1: They are found at Dhauli and Girnar, where they replace Rock Edicts XI–XIII.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the edicts are addressed to the officers of Tosali and Samapa. They are found at Dhauli and Jaugada, not Girnar; they declare 'All men are my children', while the account of the war is in Rock Edict XIII, which they omit; Jaugada is in Ganjam district, not Puri.

st.3: The Bhitari Pillar of Skandagupta is in Ghazipur district.

x: All three statements are correct: the Mehrauli Iron Pillar records Chandragupta II's conquests and stands in the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque yard; the Bhitari Pillar is in Ghazipur district, Uttar Pradesh.

st.3: Ulukudi were the tenants.

x: All three statements are correct: karanmai was the right to cultivate, mitachi the superior possessory right and ulukudi the tenants (kaniyudaiyar were the land-owning farmers).

st.1: It took place in 1299.

x: All three statements are correct: the Gujarat campaign of 1299 was led by Ulugh Khan and Nusrat Khan, and the Vaghela queen Kamala Devi was captured.

st.4: The Sayyids were called Turkan-i-Chihalgani (the Forty).
st.1: Khizr Khan took the title of Sultan and rejected the suzerainty of Timur's son Shah Rukh.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: Yahiya bin Ahmad Sarhindi wrote the Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi. Khizr Khan ruled as a deputy without the title of Sultan, accepting Shah Rukh; Mubarak Shah failed against the Khokhars; the Sayyids were called Kulah-Daran (cap-wearers), the Chihalgani being Iltutmish's Forty.

st.3: Balban's title Zil-i-Ilahi means 'Deputy of God'.
st.4: Alauddin Khalji took the titles Al-Imam and Khilafatullah.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Aibak ruled as Malik and was called Lakh Baksh. Niyabat-i-Khudai was Balban's title, Iltutmish's being Sultan-i-Azam; Zil-i-Ilahi means 'Shadow of God', not 'Deputy of God'; Al-Imam and Khilafatullah were taken by Mubarak Shah Khalji, not Alauddin.

st.1: Khanwa (1528)
st.4: Chanderi (1527)

x: Babur's battles in order: First Panipat (1526), Khanwa (1527), Chanderi (1528), Ghaghra (1529); the dates given against Khanwa and Chanderi are swapped.

st.2: The Potdar (Khazanadar) was the chief revenue collector of the pargana.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct: the Bitikchi kept land records and the Shiqdar was the executive and police officer. The Potdar was the treasurer, the revenue collector being the Amil; the Qanungo was a hereditary officer.

st.1: Moropant Pingle was the keeper of the Pune jagir and Shivaji's tutor.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: Samarth Ramdas wrote the Dasbodh. The keeper of the Pune jagir and Shivaji's tutor was Dadaji Kondadev, not Moropant Pingle; Eknath (16th century) lived before Shivaji, Tukaram being his contemporary.

st.3: Mustafanagar, one of the Circars, is also known as Rajahmundry.
st.1: Bussy obtained them from Muzaffar Jang.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the grant paid for the French troops kept by Bussy. Bussy got the Circars from Salabat Jang (Muzaffar Jang had died in 1751); Mustafanagar is Kondapalli, Rajahmundry being a separate Circar; Nellore was not one of the Circars.

st.3: After the fall of Delhi, the sons of Bahadur Shah II were shot by John Nicholson.
st.4: Rani Lakshmibai died on 17 June 1858 fighting Colin Campbell near Gwalior.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Tantia Tope was betrayed by Man Singh of Narwar. Jhansi lapsed in 1854, not 1848; the princes were shot by Hodson (Nicholson was killed in the assault); the Rani fell fighting Hugh Rose, not Colin Campbell.

st.1: Muzaffar Jang made Dupleix governor of the Mughal territory south of the Krishna.

x: All three statements are correct: Dupleix was made governor of the Mughal lands south of the Krishna; Bussy got the Northern Circars in 1753; Dupleix was recalled in 1754.

st.3: By 1758 Clive had also taken the French settlement of Chandernagore.

x: All three statements are correct: Pondicherry was the only major French base; Plassey gave the English Bengal's revenue; by 1758 Clive had taken Chandernagore in Bengal.

st.2: Company servants did not misuse dastaks, which were used only for the Company's own trade.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: weavers were forced to sell cheap to Company agents. Company servants did misuse dastaks for private trade; R.P. Dutt's mercantilist phase is 1757-1813, not 1765-1833.

st.1: They were modelled on the University of London as affiliating and examining universities.

x: All three statements are correct: the 1857 universities of Calcutta, Bombay and Madras followed the London model; Bankim Chandra was among Calcutta's first two graduates.

st.2: It recommended that education funds be spent on Western learning through English.

x: All three statements are correct: Macaulay, as Law Member and President of the GCPI, wanted funds spent on Western learning through English and a class of interpreters between rulers and ruled.

st.3: The Registration Act of 1867 was passed under Lord Lawrence.

x: All three statements are correct: Wellesley passed the 1799 Censorship Act, John Adams issued the 1823 Licensing Regulations and the 1867 Registration Act came under Lord Lawrence.

st.1: It was founded on 30 December 1906 at a session of the All-India Muhammadan Educational Conference at Aligarh.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct: Salimullah, Mohsin-ul-Mulk and Viqar-ul-Mulk took the initiative; Ameer Ali set up the London League in 1908. The founding session was at Dacca, not Aligarh; the first president was the Aga Khan, not Jinnah.

st.3: The councils created by them made the executive responsible to the legislature.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the reforms were replaced by the Act of 1919. Morley explicitly denied any aim of a parliamentary system; the councils stayed advisory and the executive was not responsible to them.

st.1: The Communist Party of India was formally founded in India at Bombay in December 1925.

x: Neither statement is correct: the CPI was founded at Kanpur, not Bombay, in December 1925; the conference was organised by Satyabhakta, not M.N. Roy.

st.1: The South Indian People's Association was formed at the Victoria Memorial Hall, Madras, in November 1920.
st.4: The symbol of the Justice Party was the Rising Sun.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: Thyagaraya Chetty signed the Non-Brahmin Manifesto. The Association was formed in November 1916, not 1920; 'Justice' was an English daily, not Tamil; the party's symbol was the Scales, not the Rising Sun.

st.1: C.P. Brown, Collector of Cuddapah, prepared Kannada-English dictionaries and edited Vemana's verses.

x: Neither statement is correct: C.P. Brown prepared Telugu-English, not Kannada-English, dictionaries; 'Life or Death: A Plea for Vernaculars' was written by P.T. Srinivasa Ayyangar, not Brown.

st.3: His Barnaparichay was a Bengali primer of the alphabet.

x: All three statements are correct: Vidyasagar became secretary of the Bethune School in 1850, opened the Sanskrit College to non-Brahmins and wrote the Bengali primer Barnaparichay.

st.1: The Calcutta session of 1928 under M.A. Ansari debated the Nehru Report and gave a one-year ultimatum.
st.3: The Karachi session of 1931, presided over by Subhas Chandra Bose, endorsed the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: Lahore 1929 under Jawaharlal Nehru adopted Purna Swaraj. Calcutta 1928 was presided over by Motilal Nehru, not Ansari; Karachi 1931 by Vallabhbhai Patel, not Bose; the Fundamental Rights resolution came at Karachi 1931, not Lahore.

st.2: Members could discuss the budget and also move amendments to it.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the Act came under Lansdowne. Members could discuss the budget but could not vote on or amend it; election was only indirect.

st.1: It was tried in the ordinary court of the Lahore Sessions Judge.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct: sentence was passed in October 1930 and Kishori Lal got transportation for life. The case went before a special tribunal set up by the Governor-General's ordinance, not an ordinary court; Sukhdev and Rajguru, not Batukeshwar Dutt, were hanged with Bhagat Singh.

st.4: The English Nil Darpan was published by Harish Chandra Mukherjee.
st.3: The Indigo Commission (1860) held that ryots were bound to fulfil future indigo contracts.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the revolt was led by the Biswas brothers of Nadia. Nil Darpan was translated by Michael Madhusudan Dutt, not Dinabandhu Mitra (its author); the Commission held ryots could refuse future contracts; the translation was published by Rev. James Long.

st.1: The CPI supported it, as it still called the war an 'Imperialist War' after Germany attacked the USSR.
st.4: The Unionist Party of Punjab actively supported it.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: the RSS kept away. The CPI opposed it, calling the war a 'People's War' after the attack on the USSR; the Hindu Mahasabha and the Unionist Party did not support it.

st.3: He founded the Natal Indian Congress in 1894.

x: All three statements are correct: Gandhi studied at Samaldas College and the Inner Temple, went to South Africa in 1893 and founded the Natal Indian Congress in 1894.

st.3: At Machilipatnam the auctioned salt was bought by Puranam Suri Sastry.

x: All three statements are correct: Kaleswara Rao led the Machilipatnam satyagraha on 6 April 1930, Prakasam and Nageswara Rao the first Madras squad, and Puranam Suri Sastry bought the auctioned salt.

st.3: The Sardar Patel National Unity Award (2019) is a medal and citation, with no cash prize.

x: All three statements are correct: Rashtriya Ekta Diwas (31 October) was announced in 2014; the Statue of Unity was unveiled on 31 October 2018; the Unity Award carries no cash and is open to any citizen or institution.

st.3: Mandal Praja Parishads replaced Panchayat Samitis by an Act of 1986.

x: All three statements are correct: AP adopted Panchayati Raj on 1 November 1959, second after Rajasthan, and the 1986 Act replaced Panchayat Samitis with Mandal Praja Parishads.

st.1: It demanded an Andhra State but opposed a separate Andhra University.

x: Neither statement is correct: the movement demanded both an Andhra State and an Andhra University, and it promoted Telugu in education and administration.

st.1: It was formed on 1 November 1953 as the first linguistic state.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct: Nehru inaugurated it at Kurnool; the Bill got assent on 14 September 1953. It was formed on 1 October, not 1 November, 1953; Vizianagaram was not then a district (formed in 1979).

st.3: No major change in the Mulki rules followed the 1952 inquiry.

x: All three statements are correct: the 1919 farman tightened the Mulki rules to about 15 years' residence, and the 1952 inquiry brought no major change in them.

st.3: It won 10 of the 14 Lok Sabha seats in 1971 and merged with the Congress in September 1971 after an agreement with P.V. Narasimha Rao.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the TPS was formed in February 1969 with A. Madan Mohan as convener and the spade as symbol. The 1971 merger followed an agreement with Indira Gandhi, not P.V. Narasimha Rao; the Complete TPS was led by B. Satyanarayana Reddy, not K. Jayashankar.

st.1: It was led by Kakani Venkataratnam and B.V. Subba Reddy.

x: All three statements are correct: Jai Andhra was led by Kakani Venkataratnam, B.V. Subba Reddy and Tenneti Viswanatham, with students at its core, against Andhras being treated as outsiders in Hyderabad.

st.1: The Malwa culture is dated to 1400–700 BCE.
st.2: The Jorwe culture is dated to 1900–1400 BCE.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: Inamgaon is a Jorwe site in the Pravara–Godavari zone. The dates are swapped: Malwa is 1900–1400 BCE and Jorwe 1400–700 BCE; Navdatoli was excavated by H.D. Sankalia, not V.N. Misra.

st.3: The Belum Caves are the second-longest cave system in the Indian subcontinent.

x: All three statements are correct: the Billa Surgam caves are in Betamcherla mandal and were explored by Robert Bruce Foote in 1884; Belum is the second-longest cave system, after Meghalaya's Krem Liat Prah.

st.1: Gautami Balasri gave a cave vihara at Nasik to the Mahasanghika monks.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct: Lilavati was Hala's queen and Naganika was the daughter of Tranakayiro. Gautami Balasri's Nasik cave went to the Bhadrayaniya monks, not the Mahasanghikas; the regent was Naganika, not Gautami Balasri.

st.3: The centre of the Siddharthika sect was Guntupalli.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the Chaitika sects were founded by Mahadeva Bhikshu. They were branches of the Mahasanghikas, not the Theravadins; the Siddharthika centre was Gudivada, not Guntupalli.

st.1: Ceylonese monks made Nagarjunakonda their base for Hinayana.

x: All three statements are correct: Ceylonese monks used Nagarjunakonda as a Hinayana base; Mahadeva Bhikshu took Buddhism from Pallava-bhoga to Sri Lanka; Hiuen Tsang found the Sriparvata vihara neglected.

st.3: Dantamukha Swami (Ganapati) was installed at Velpuru in the 33rd regnal year of Madhava Varma II.

x: All three statements are correct: Madhava Varma II performed 11 Ashvamedhas; Sriparvataswami is Srisaila Mallikarjuna; Dantamukha Swami was installed at Velpuru in his 33rd year.

st.1: Bhairavakona has eight rock-cut Jain caves.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct: Mogalrajapuram is at Vijayawada and the Vishnukundins began Hindu cave temples in the Pallava style. Bhairavakona's eight caves are Shiva shrines, not Jain; Undavalli was cut by the Vishnukundins, not the Cholas.

st.2: Mangalesha ruled after Kirtivarman I.

x: All three statements are correct: the order is Pulakesin I, Kirtivarman I, Mangalesha, and later Vikramaditya I.

st.3: Telugu rose as a literary language under their patronage.

x: All three statements are correct: Sanskrit was the Eastern Chalukyas' official language and most of their about 100 grants are in it, while Telugu rose as a literary language under their patronage.

st.3: Dhanunjaya Varma ruled from Chimbapuram (Chimamburu).

x: All three statements are correct: Renadu lay where Kadapa, Kurnool and Chittoor meet, in the upper Pennar basin; Dhanunjaya Varma ruled from Chimbapuram.

st.1: The title Rayagajakesari
st.2: The Sanigaram inscription
st.3: Introduction of the Nayankara system

x: None of these is associated with Ganapatideva: Rayagajakesari was Rudramadevi's title; the Sanigaram inscription is of Prolaraja; the Nayankara system was introduced by Prataparudra; the Kesari Samudram tank was built by Prola I.

st.2: The Rashtra (Mandala) was the largest administrative unit.

x: All three statements are correct: Malyala Hemadri Reddi and Muppidi Nayudu were prime ministers; the Rashtra/Mandala was the largest unit, above the Nadu; the 72 Niyogas were under the Bahattara Niyogadhipati.

st.3: Land revenue, collected through tax farming, was the main source of income.

x: All three statements are correct: Machilipatnam was leased for 1,80,000 pagodas; diamond-mine leases and port customs added income; land revenue, farmed to the highest bidder, was the main source.

st.1: The viceroy line ended with Parantaka Chola.

x: All three statements are correct: the viceroy line ended with Parantaka Chola; Vikrama Chola was recalled in 1118 as co-regent; the nadu vassals later accepted Velanadu and then the Kakatiyas.

st.3: The Kakatiyas actively persecuted the Lingayats.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: followers are Lingayats and gurus Jangamas. Veerashaivism rejected the Vedas and caste; the Kakatiyas stayed neutral and did not persecute the Lingayats.

st.1: Devadaya were lands granted to Brahmins as agraharas.
st.4: The main revenue of the state was the tax on trade.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the Sri Bhandara was kept by the Karanam. Devadaya were temple villages and endowments, not Brahmin agraharas; the Samayas met in temple mandapas, not the palace; the main state revenue was the land tax.

st.3: The stellate plan is a raised circular platform.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the sandbox foundation used pits of sand, stone chips and earth. Kirtimukha is the 'face of glory' motif, not monolithic carving; the stellate plan is star-shaped, not circular.

st.1: The 300 cattle driven into the forest without paying the tax were impounded at Minchalapadu.

x: All three statements are correct: the 300 cattle were impounded at Minchalapadu; the pullari was 12 annas a cow under the 1878 Act; Kanneganti Hanumanthu was shot there in February 1922.

st.1: P. Sundarayya hailed from Alaganipadu in Guntur district.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct: Sundarayya was AP's first Leader of the Opposition and Ravi Narayana Reddy won Nalgonda in 1952 with India's highest majority. Alaganipadu is in Nellore, not Guntur; 'Visalandhralo Prajarajyam' was written by Sundarayya, not Ravi Narayana Reddy.

st.1: It was founded at Sorugu, near Jammalamadugu, in Kadapa district.

x: All three statements are correct: Surabhi was founded at Sorugu in Kadapa (1885) by a leather-puppet family that turned to live actors, and its first play was Keechaka Vadham.

st.3: According to NextGen, Krowidi Lingaraju was jailed for two years for the playlet 'Chichula Pidugu'.
st.4: Madduri Annapurnayya was punished for the editorial 'Veerabali'.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: Harisarvottama Rao was the first Telugu editor jailed in the Vandemataram movement. The 1878 Act was repealed by Ripon, not Curzon; Lingaraju was jailed for the editorial 'Veerabali' and Annapurnayya for the playlet 'Chichula Pidugu', not the other way round.

st.1: The National Mission on Libraries is run by the Ministry of Education.
st.2: Its nodal agency is the National Book Trust.
st.4: The Amaravati Central Library is planned with IIT Bombay.

x: None of the statements is correct: the Mission is run by the Ministry of Culture with the RRRLF as nodal agency; AP plans model libraries in all 175 constituencies within three years, not five; the Amaravati Central Library is with the Global Institute of Good Governance, IIT Bombay leading the National Virtual Library.

st.4: He opposed the AP Public Libraries Act, 1960, as a curb on village libraries.
st.1: Viswanatha Satyanarayana called him the 'University of Humanity' and 'Walking Library'.
st.2: He received the Kala Prapoorna from Sri Venkateswara University in 1975.

x: None of the statements is correct about Pathuri Nagabhushanam: the titles came from Karunasri (Jandhyala Papayya Sastri); the Kala Prapoorna (1975) came from Andhra University; he set up about 160 village libraries as Secretary of the Guntur, not Krishna, Library Association; he sat on the drafting committee of the 1960 Act.

st.2: Eenadu was started at Vijayawada in 1974.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: K.L.N. Prasad founded Andhra Jyothi in 1960. Eenadu began at Visakhapatnam, not Vijayawada; the first communist Telugu journal was Prajasakti, Jaya Bharat being the first after Independence.

st.3: The International Telugu Institute was set up in 1975.

x: All three statements are correct: the AP Sahitya Akademi dates from 1957, the national Sahitya Akademi from 1954 and the International Telugu Institute from 1975.

st.1: It remained subordinate to the British Parliament.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: it continued as the Provisional Parliament till 1952. It became a fully sovereign body; Rajendra Prasad chaired it as constitution-maker and Mavalankar as Dominion Legislature, not the reverse.

st.3: The Muslim League boycotted the first sitting.

x: All three statements are correct: Rajendra Prasad was elected permanent President on 11 December 1946, H.C. Mukherjee was a Vice-President and the Muslim League boycotted the first sitting.

st.3: The Ashtadhyayi mentions twenty-two janapadas.

x: All three statements are correct: Panini was born at Pushkalavati; the Ashtadhyayi has eight chapters and names 22 janapadas.

st.3: Jarasandha of the Brihadratha line ruled from Girivraja (Rajagriha).

x: All three statements are correct: Magadha was the most powerful Mahajanapada; its first dynasty was the Brihadratha, and Jarasandha ruled from Girivraja.

st.1: It was discovered in 1993 near Bamiyan in Afghanistan.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: the Rabatak inscription gives Kujula – Vima Taktu – Vima Kadphises – Kanishka. It was found near Surkh Kotal, not Bamiyan; it is in Bactrian in the Greek, not Kharoshthi, script.

st.1: Tolkappiyam has three parts - Aram, Porul and Inbam.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct: the Kural has 1,330 couplets and is called Ulaga Podhumarai. Tolkappiyam's parts are Ezhuttu, Col and Porul, while Aram, Porul and Inbam are the Kural's books; the Porul book deals with wealth and polity, love being Inbam.

st.1: The Bihar caste survey (2 October 2023) put Extremely Backward Classes at 27% and OBCs at 36%.
st.4: Karnataka's SEEEPC report (April 2026) found SCs and STs three times more backward than the general castes.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: Census 2027 is the first digital Census and first caste count since 1931. Bihar put EBCs at 36% and OBCs at 27%; AP was the second State, after Bihar; the SEEEPC report is Telangana's, not Karnataka's.

st.4: The 106th Amendment quota in the Lok Sabha came into force with the 2024 general election.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Articles 243D and 243T reserve one-third for women in Panchayats and Municipalities. Articles 330A and 332A reserve one-third, not one-half; the 106th Amendment quota waits for the Census and delimitation.

st.4: Under Article 338(9), the Union and States may consult the NCSC on major policy matters affecting SCs at their discretion.
st.2: The NCST Chairperson holds the rank of a Minister of State.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: each Commission has a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and three members. The NCST Chairperson has Cabinet rank; reports go to the President, not directly to Parliament; consultation under Article 338(9) is mandatory.

st.3: About 23.3% of women were married before 18.

x: All three statements are correct as per NFHS-5: 32% of ever-married women faced spousal violence, 29% of women aged 18-49 physical violence, and 23.3% were married before 18.

st.3: Andhra Pradesh ranked first in its implementation in the first 45 days.

x: All three statements are correct: the Mission is run by the Ministry of Rural Development, sets a ₹300 wage floor with 60:40 funding (90:10 for NE/Himalayan States), and AP ranked first in the first 45 days.

st.3: SHREYAS supports SC students in school education up to Class XII.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: PM-YASASVI covers OBC, EBC and DNT students below Rs 2.5 lakh. It earmarks 30%, not 33%, of slots for girls; SHREYAS supports SC students in higher education such as IITs and IIMs, not schooling.

st.2: 'Relief of the disabled and unemployable' is Entry 9 of the State List.

x: All three statements are correct: Article 41 covers public assistance in disablement; the subject is Entry 9 of the State List; India has ratified the UNCRPD but not its Optional Protocol.

st.4: The US doubled its duty on Indian goods to 50 per cent in August 2025 as a penalty for India's purchases of Iranian oil.
st.1: Chinese nationals receive about 71 per cent of approved US H-1B visas.
st.3: A fee of $100,000 on renewals of existing H-1B visas applies from 21 September 2025.

x: None of the statements is correct: Indians, not Chinese, get about 71% of H-1Bs; GSP benefits were withdrawn in June 2019, not 2017; the $100,000 fee applies to new petitions, not renewals; the 50% duty (27 August 2025) penalised purchases of Russian, not Iranian, oil.

st.3: Article IV consultations are held only with members that borrow from the IMF.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the IMFC advises the Board of Governors. India is a founding member of the IMF, not a post-1991 entrant; Article IV consultations are a regular review of every member's economy, borrower or not.

st.4: Belarus joined at the New Delhi (virtual) Summit of July 2023.
st.1: Its Secretariat is at Tashkent and its RATS at Beijing.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: India and Pakistan became full members in 2017 at Astana. The Secretariat is at Beijing and RATS at Tashkent; Belarus joined at Astana in July 2024 (Iran joined in 2023) and is the newest member.

st.1: It means a strict wall of separation between state and religion, as in the USA.
st.2: Article 326 bars exclusion from electoral rolls on grounds of religion.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: the Constituent Assembly rejected including 'God'. Indian secularism means equal respect for all religions, not a US-style wall of separation; the bar is in Article 325, not 326; 'Secular' was added by the 42nd, not the 44th, Amendment.

st.3: The Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) held that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution, reversing Berubari.

x: All three statements are correct: Kesavananda Bharati was decided by 13 judges, held the Preamble a part of the Constitution and amendable without destroying its basic features.

st.2: It is available only to citizens.
st.1: It is enforced through Article 32 as well as Article 226.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: in GGR Housing (2026) the AP High Court insisted on strict due process under Article 300A. As a legal right it is enforced under Article 226 or by suit, not Article 32; it is available to any person, including non-citizens and companies; Kesavananda did not make property a basic feature.

st.3: The State may take away the minority character of an institution that receives State aid.
st.1: Clause (2) is described as the 'Charter of Education Rights'.

x: None of the statements is correct: it is clause (1) that is called the 'Charter of Education Rights'; the right belongs to religious and linguistic minorities; the State may regulate standards but may not take away minority character, aided or not.

st.4: A right that is not a Fundamental Right, such as the right to vote, is enforced in the Supreme Court under Article 32.
st.3: Since the 42nd Amendment (1976), a High Court may issue writs beyond its territory if the cause of action arises within it.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the Article 32 remedy is itself a Fundamental Right, while Article 226 is discretionary. Article 226 also covers 'any other purpose'; the extra-territorial writ power came by the 15th Amendment (1963); non-Fundamental rights are enforced under Article 226, not 32.

st.4: Article 39A is the last Directive Principle to be added.
st.1: Article 38(2) was added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: the First Amendment added the Ninth Schedule. Article 38(2) came by the 44th Amendment (1978); Article 43B came by the 97th Amendment (2011), not the 42nd, and it is the last Directive Principle added.

st.2: Minerva Mills upheld the 42nd Amendment's extension of it to all Directive Principles.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: Minerva Mills held Emergency proclamations open to judicial review. Kesavananda struck down Article 31C's second provision (barring judicial review), not its first; Minerva Mills struck down its extension to all Directive Principles.

st.3: The 103rd Amendment provided 10% EWS reservation.

x: All three statements are correct: the 93rd Amendment inserted Article 15(5), the 96th changed 'Oriya' to 'Odia' and the 103rd gave 10% EWS reservation.

st.3: The first no-confidence motion in the Lok Sabha was moved by A.K. Gopalan against Jawaharlal Nehru in 1963.
st.1: In November 1954 Gouthu Latchanna's no-confidence motion against the Bezawada Gopala Reddy ministry of Andhra State was carried 69–68.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: President's Rule came in Andhra State in November 1954. The 1954 motion felled the Prakasam ministry (Gopala Reddy became CM in 1955); the first Lok Sabha motion was moved by J.B. Kripalani; notice is given in writing to the Secretary-General, not the Speaker.

st.2: The oath of office of the President is administered by the Chief Justice of India.

x: All three statements are correct: under Article 59 the President cannot sit in any legislature and gets a rent-free residence; the oath is administered by the Chief Justice of India; he swears to preserve, protect and defend the Constitution and the law.

st.2: An amnesty falls outside Article 72.

x: All three statements are correct: Article 72 covers court-martial sentences, Union-law offences and every death sentence; amnesty falls outside it; Maru Ram (1980) held the power is exercised on the Council of Ministers' advice.

st.2: If a returned Bill is passed again, with or without amendment, he may withhold his assent once more.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct: no time limit is fixed, and a Bill derogating from the High Court's powers must be reserved. A Money Bill cannot be returned; a Bill passed again after return must receive his assent.

st.1: He communicates to the Governor only the decisions of the Council of Ministers on legislation, not on administration.
st.3: The Chief Secretary is the chief link between the Governor and the Council of Ministers.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: seeking information from the CM is a constitutional discretion of the Governor. The CM communicates all decisions on administration and legislation; the CM, not the Chief Secretary, is the chief link; an individual Minister's decision goes to the Council only if the Governor so requires.

st.3: In S.R. Bommai (1994) the Supreme Court held that their decisions can be reviewed on grounds of mala fides.

x: All three statements are correct: ministerial advice to the Governor cannot be inquired into (Article 163(3)); Article 361 protects the President and Governor; Bommai held their decisions reviewable for mala fides.

st.2: An appeal against its order on a substantial question of law lies to the Supreme Court within 90 days.

x: All three statements are correct: TDSAT hears telecom, broadcasting and airport tariff disputes; appeals on substantial questions of law go to the Supreme Court within 90 days; the Cyber Appellate Tribunal was merged into it in 2017.

st.2: The resolution remains in force for up to one year and cannot be renewed.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the Rajya Sabha passes it by two-thirds of members present and voting. It lasts up to one year but can be renewed any number of times; the Lok Sabha has no role.

st.1: China is the world's biggest executioner, according to its officially published figures.
st.2: Executions were carried out in 53 countries in 2017.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: at least 2,707 executions (excluding China) were recorded in 2025, the highest since 1981. China is the biggest executioner, but its figures are a state secret; executions took place in 23 countries in 2017; Iran, not Saudi Arabia, led in 2025.

st.2: Article 21 of the UDHR (1948) recognises the right to seek and receive information.
st.4: Norway's Freedom of the Press Act, 1766 is regarded as the world's first RTI law.
st.3: Rajasthan (1997) was the first Indian State to have an RTI law.

x: None of the statements is correct: the FOI Act 2002 was never notified before its repeal in 2005; the right is in Article 19 of the UDHR; Tamil Nadu (with Goa) was first, in 1997; the 1766 law is Sweden's.

st.3: It has been published every two years since 1995.
st.2: On its 0-100 scale, a score of 100 denotes 'highly corrupt'.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the index comes from Transparency International, Berlin. A score of 0 means 'highly corrupt' and 100 'very clean'; it has been published every year since 1995; it measures perceived public-sector corruption, not court cases.

st.1: Its study team on Centre-State relations was headed by K. Hanumanthaiah.
st.2: Its 1979 report on Centre-State relations made 22 recommendations.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: the First ARC asked for an Inter-State Council under Article 263. Its study team was headed by M.C. Setalvad (Hanumanthaiah chaired the ARC itself); its report came in 1969; most recommendations were not implemented.

st.2: Under one route, either 6% of valid votes in four or more States or at least 4 Lok Sabha seats is enough.
st.4: A party recognised as a State party in four or more States qualifies as a national party only if it also wins 4 Lok Sabha seats.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the conditions are in Paragraph 6B of the 1968 Order. Under the first route the 6% vote share and 4 seats are both required; the 2% route needs members from at least three States; recognition as a State party in four States is enough by itself.

st.1: The term 'democratic decentralisation' was coined by the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee.

x: All three statements are correct: the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee coined the term; participation and decentralisation are the objects of Panchayati Raj; effective PRIs need decentralisation of decision-making, administration and the system, not judicial powers.

st.3: Section 29 and the Sixth Schedule of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 amended the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950 for Andhra Pradesh.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: AP gave effect to PESA through the 1998 amendment Act. Under the AP PESA Rules, 2011 the Gram Panchayat, not the Mandal Parishad, acts as the market committee; the 2014 change was made by the AP Reorganisation Act, not the 1956 Act.

st.1: State laws inconsistent with PESA lapse one year after the President's assent to PESA.

x: All three statements are correct: inconsistent State laws lapse after one year; a Gram Sabha may be at habitation level; the Gram Sabha or Panchayat can prevent and reverse tribal land alienation.

st.1: It is measured on a 0-1 scale on which 1 denotes parity.
st.2: Its reproductive health dimension includes the maternal mortality ratio and the sex ratio at birth.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: India ranked 102nd in the GII (HDR 2025). On the GII 1 denotes the worst position, not parity; its reproductive health dimension uses MMR and the adolescent birth rate; reproductive health is not a Global Gender Gap sub-index.

st.1: G.O. Rt. No. 1065 (August 2026) provides 33.33 per cent BC reservation in Andhra Pradesh rural local bodies.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct: VMRDA replaced VUDA in 2018 and APCRDA (2014) plans Amaravati. G.O. 1065 gives the BC quota in urban, not rural, local bodies; the Cabinet approved direct, not indirect, election of Mayors.

st.2: Ind AS 117 and Ind AS 109 replace IFRS for insurers.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Section 16A creates the Policyholders' Education and Protection Fund. Ind AS 117 and 109 replace IGAAP (Ind AS being converged with IFRS); HDFC Bank is a D-SIB, the D-SIIs being LIC, GIC Re and New India Assurance.

st.2: Gujarat topped NITI Aayog's Investment Friendliness Index 2026.

x: All three statements are correct: DARPG publishes GRAI; Gujarat topped the Investment Friendliness Index 2026; India ranked 16th of 154 in the Responsible Nations Index 2026.

st.2: India became a full member of the SCO in 2005.
st.3: The African Union was made a permanent member of the G20 during Brazil's Presidency.
st.1: The Quad, first formed in 2007, was revived in 2020.

x: None of the statements is correct: the Quad was revived in 2017; India became an SCO observer in 2005 and a full member in 2017; the African Union joined the G20 under India's 2023 Presidency; Neighbourhood First dates from 2014.

st.3: Its Memorandum of Agreement was signed in December 2024.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Ken-Betwa is the first NPP link implemented, between MP and UP. Its MoA was signed in March 2021 (the foundation stone came in December 2024); the Daudhan Dam lies in Panna, not Kanha, Tiger Reserve.

st.3: The Twelfth Schedule lists 18 functions for municipalities, which do not include police.

x: All three statements are correct: property tax is the main own revenue of ULBs; the Economic Survey 2016-17 used Bengaluru imagery; the Twelfth Schedule has 18 functions and excludes police.

st.1: GHTC-India was launched in 2021 by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.

x: All three statements are correct: MoHUA launched GHTC-India in 2021; the Light House Projects were founded in January 2021 at six cities; VAMBAY (2001) was merged into BSUP.

st.2: AP's per capita income is based on GSDP.

x: Neither statement is correct: AP's GSDP is compiled by the State DES, not the NSO; per capita income is based on NSDP, not GSDP.

st.1: As per the NCEUS, informal workers include only unorganised-sector workers, not organised-sector workers without social security.

x: Neither statement is correct: the NCEUS counts organised-sector workers without social security as informal too; informal employment is the large majority of India's workforce, not less than half.

st.2: This cost arises mainly through lower export earnings.
st.3: About one-third of the world's rivers have been dammed or diverted.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the World Bank put the cost at about 5.7% of GDP (Rs 3.75 lakh crore, 2009). It arises through higher healthcare spending and lower labour productivity; more than 60% of rivers are dammed or diverted; about 40%, not 10%, of land is degraded.

st.1: World Data Lab (2018) estimated that the Democratic Republic of Congo may have overtaken India as the country with the most extreme poor.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct: World Data Lab runs the Poverty Clock; Indians below $4.20 a day fell from 57.7% to 23.9%. World Data Lab named Nigeria, not DR Congo; global extreme poverty at $2.15 is about 9.2%, not 19%.

st.1: In 2023-24 Uttar Pradesh had the lowest and Goa the highest per capita NSDP.
st.3: The Godavari delta and Krishna districts lag in Andhra Pradesh's intra-State disparities.

x: None of the statements is correct: Bihar, not Uttar Pradesh, had the lowest per capita NSDP; AP's district MPI gaps measure intra-State inequality; Rayalaseema and North Coastal districts lag, not the delta.

st.1: Frictional unemployment is long-term, lasting until the worker is reskilled.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: structural unemployment needs reskilling or reform. Frictional unemployment is short-term job-search unemployment and exists even at full employment.

st.4: The Gandhian and Sarvodaya plans offered a centralised, heavy-industry alternative.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: industrialists prepared the Bombay Plan; Ardeshir Dalal headed the 1944 department. M.N. Roy wrote the People's Plan and did not sign the Bombay Plan; the Gandhian and Sarvodaya plans were decentralised.

st.2: Andhra Pradesh's Swarna Andhra Vision 2047 targets a GSDP of Rs 308.11 lakh crore by 2035-36.
st.3: Swarna Andhra Vision 2047 has ten guiding principles called 'Navaratnalu'.

x: None of the statements is correct: the 1985-2000 perspective plan accompanied the Seventh, not Sixth, Plan; the Rs 308.11 lakh crore target is for 2047-48; the ten principles are the 'Padi Sutralu', not 'Navaratnalu'.

st.3: The First Plan succeeded mainly because of heavy investment in basic industries.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: a high capital-output ratio needs more capital per unit of output. Low growth despite high savings points to a high, not low, ratio; the First Plan's success owed mainly to good harvests, heavy industry being the Second Plan's thrust.

st.3: The size of the Eleventh Plan was Rs 36,44,718 crore.

x: All three statements are correct: the Twelfth Plan's IMR target was 25; the Eleventh Plan had 27 monitorable targets (13 at State level) and a size of Rs 36,44,718 crore.

st.1: Delicensed firms got pricing freedom but remained subject to MRTP curbs on expansion.
st.3: The BIFR was set up to clear foreign investment proposals.

x: None of the statements is correct: delicensed firms got pricing freedom and no curbs on expansion; automatic approval was for FDI up to 51%, not 74%; the BIFR was set up to revive sick units, foreign proposals going to the FIPB.

st.4: It runs the PM-KISAN scheme.
st.1: AIM 2.0, approved in 2024 with Rs 2,750 crore, runs up to March 2030.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: NITI's two hubs are the Team India Hub and the Knowledge and Innovation Hub. AIM 2.0 runs to March 2028; the SETU Steering Committee is chaired by the CEO; NITI runs the Aspirational Districts Programme, PM-KISAN being an Agriculture Ministry scheme.

st.4: The Reserve Bank Integrated Ombudsman Scheme 2026 covers only scheduled commercial banks.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Payments Regulatory Board has six members, three of them Government nominees, and is chaired by the Governor. It replaced the Board for Regulation and Supervision of Payment and Settlement Systems, not the BFS; RB-IOS 2026 ('One Nation One Ombudsman') also covers RRBs, UCBs, NBFCs and payment operators.

st.3: IDBI Bank was reclassified as a private sector bank after LIC took majority control in 2019.

x: All three statements are correct: ICICI (1955) was the second all-India industrial FI; IDBI (1964) began as an RBI subsidiary; IDBI Bank became a private sector bank after LIC's 2019 takeover.

st.3: The merger of New Bank of India into Bank of Baroda in 1993 brought the number of nationalised banks down to 19.
st.2: Morarji Desai's note on the subject was titled 'Stray Thoughts on Bank Nationalisation'.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the 14 banks of 1969 held about 85% of deposits. 'Stray Thoughts' was Indira Gandhi's note, not Morarji Desai's; New Bank of India merged into PNB, not Bank of Baroda; after the 2019-20 mergers India has 12 public sector banks.

st.2: Under the SBI (Subsidiary Banks) Act, 1959, eight princely-state banks became SBI associates.

x: All three statements are correct: SBI was formed on 1 July 1955 with the RBI holding about 92%; eight princely-state banks became associates in 1959; the Government took the RBI's 59.7% stake in 2007.

st.1: It raised the tenure of co-operative bank directors from 8 years to 10 years.

x: All three statements are correct: the Act, in force from 1 August 2025, raised co-operative bank directors' tenure from 8 to 10 years and the 'substantial interest' limit from ₹5 lakh to ₹2 crore.

st.1: Narasimham-II, set up in 1991, proposed three tiers: 2-3 international banks, 8-10 national banks and many local banks.
st.4: Narasimham-I recommended raising priority-sector lending to 40% of bank credit.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: Narasimham-II favoured fewer, stronger banks. Narasimham-II was the 1998 committee (Narasimham-I was 1991); Narasimham-I asked for SLR to fall from 38.5% to 25%, not 15%, and for directed credit to be cut to 10%, not raised.

st.2: It is a statutory body set up under the CGST Act, 2017.

x: Neither statement is correct: the GST Council is chaired by the Union Finance Minister, not a Minister of State; it is a constitutional body under Article 279A, never a statutory one.

st.1: Viability gap funding for harnessing floating solar energy, for an initial capacity of 1 GW.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: coal gasification and liquefaction of 100 MT by 2030 was proposed. The 1 GW VGF was for offshore wind, not floating solar; CBG blending in CNG and PNG was to be phased mandatory, not optional.

st.2: China was India's largest export destination in 2024-25.
st.3: In FY 2025-26 the UAE became India's largest trading partner, overtaking the USA.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: India had surpluses with the USA and the Netherlands. The largest surplus ($35.32 bn) was with the USA, not the UAE; China was the largest import source while the USA is the top export market; in 2025-26 China, not the UAE, became the largest trading partner again.

st.4: India's FTAs are credited with turning deficits with ASEAN, Japan and Korea into surpluses.
st.1: CEPA stands for Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: India had 14 FTAs and 6 PTAs in April 2026. CEPA is a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement, CECA being the Cooperation Agreement; SAFTA added Afghanistan, the Maldives being an original SAPTA member; the FTAs are criticised for widening deficits with ASEAN, Japan and Korea.

st.2: It is run by the CBIC.
st.1: It has an outlay of ₹25,060 crore for FY 2021-22 to 2025-26.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: the Mission is meant mainly for MSMEs and first-time exporters. Its ₹25,060 crore covers FY 2025-26 to 2030-31; it is run by the DGFT, CBIC running RoDTEP; it merges the Interest Equalisation Scheme and the Market Access Initiative, not RoDTEP.

st.3: Chit funds and Nidhi companies are prohibited for FDI.

x: All three statements are correct: railway infrastructure allows 100% automatic FDI; railway operations (barring permitted activities), chit funds and Nidhi companies are prohibited.

st.3: Rainfed farming covers about 20% of the net sown area and gives about 40% of food output.
st.1: Sustainable agriculture puts meeting present needs first, even at some cost to the land's quality for future generations.
st.2: Its pillars are environmental health, economic profitability and maximum mechanisation.

x: None of the statements is correct: sustainable agriculture keeps land quality intact for future generations; its pillars are environmental health, economic profitability and social and economic equity; rainfed farming covers 50-60% of the net sown area; the NRAA was set up in 2006, not 2010.

st.4: The AP (Andhra Area) Tenancy Act, 1956 was based on the Kumarappa Committee.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: under the 1950 Hyderabad Act six years' cultivation made a protected tenant, who could buy the land at 60% of market price in 20 instalments. The 1956 Andhra Act capped rent at 30% for wet and 25% for dry land, not the reverse, and was based on the Subba Rao Committee, not Kumarappa.

st.3: NABARD, the apex rural development bank, was set up in 1982.

x: All three statements are correct: the AIRCS Committee (1951) was chaired by A.D. Gorwala; SBI was created from the Imperial Bank on 1 July 1955; NABARD was set up in 1982.

st.3: Under VB-G RAM G, Andhra Pradesh offers 125 days of wage work in distressed pockets.

x: All three statements are correct: NREGA came into force in 2006 and became MGNREGA in 2009; it has been replaced by VB-G RAM G, under which AP offers 125 days in distressed pockets.

st.3: The CACP considers only domestic price trends, not international markets.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the Swaminathan Commission recommended C2 + 50%. Since 2018-19 MSP is at least 1.5 times A2+FL, not C2; the CACP considers both domestic and international price trends.

st.1: The Agricultural Prices Commission was renamed CACP in 1991.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: the CACP has a Chairman, a Member Secretary, one official and two non-official members. The APC was renamed CACP in 1985; it is an attached office of the Agriculture Ministry, not a statutory body.

st.4: A delicensed unit needs prior approval from the DPIIT before it starts production.
st.2: At present, compulsory industrial licensing applies to four industries (DPIIT Press Note 3, 2019 Series), including alcoholic drinks.
st.1: Automobiles, white goods and leather were delicensed in 2004.

x: None of the statements is correct: automobiles, white goods and leather were delicensed in 1993; alcoholic drinks are no longer in the four-industry licensing list; drugs and pharmaceuticals were delicensed earlier; a delicensed unit only files an IEM.

st.2: It provided for a mixed economy, defining the spheres of the public and private sectors.

x: All three statements are correct: Shyama Prasad Mukherjee announced the 1948 Resolution; it set up a mixed economy with defined public and private spheres; arms, atomic energy and railways were Central monopolies.

st.1: B-READY, the IMF's successor to Doing Business, rests on three pillars – regulatory framework, public services and operational efficiency.
st.2: Starting a business and getting electricity were India's weakest Doing Business indicators.

x: Neither statement is correct: B-READY is the World Bank's successor to Doing Business, not the IMF's; India's weakest indicators were enforcing contracts and registering property.

st.1: India's share of world services trade fell from 4.3% in 2005 to 2% in 2024.

x: Neither statement is correct: India's share rose from 2% (2005) to 4.3% (2024); in 2024-25 services exports ($387.5 bn) far exceeded imports ($198.7 bn).

st.1: It is the services counterpart of the Wholesale Price Index.
st.4: The first trial index was compiled for April 2025.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: the ISP is monthly, released within 60 days. It is the services counterpart of the IIP, not the WPI; its base year is 2024-25, not 2011-12; the first trial index was for April 2026.

st.2: The 'employment-output paradox' of the services sector was highlighted by NITI Aayog.

x: All three statements are correct: in 2021-22 services gave 53.89% of GDP but 33.80% of jobs; NITI Aayog highlighted this paradox; about 51.5% of service workers get regular wages.

st.1: It was 38.1% of the allotment in 2015-16.

x: Neither statement is correct: fertiliser use was 80.78% of the allotment in 2015-16 and fell to 38.1% in 2016-17 (AE).

st.1: GSDP estimates move through the stages AE/FAE → SRE → FRE → TRE.
st.3: AP's real growth for 2024-25 was revised from 8.27% (FAE) to 9.24% (FRE).

x: Only statement 4 is correct: MoSPI's new GDP series (February 2026) has base 2022-23. The cycle is AE/FAE → FRE → SRE → TRE; AP still uses 2011-12 prices, not 2004-05; 2024-25 growth was revised from 9.24% (FAE) down to 8.27% (FRE).

st.2: Agriculture had the largest current-price GVA, ₹6.11 lakh crore.
st.1: GSDP was ₹15.91 lakh crore at constant prices and ₹8.67 lakh crore at current prices.

x: None of the statements is correct: GSDP was ₹15.91 lakh crore at current and ₹8.67 lakh crore at constant prices; services, not agriculture, had the largest current GVA (₹6.11 lakh crore); AP ranked 8th, not 10th.

st.3: The Bill replacing it was passed by the Lok Sabha in June 2016.
st.1: It moved the submergence villages and mandals of Warangal district to Andhra Pradesh to ease resettlement.
st.4: As a result Telangana's area rose from 1,60,205 sq km to 1,62,970 sq km.

x: None of the statements is correct: the Ordinance moved Khammam's, not Warangal's, submergence villages to AP; the base rule excluded villages in G.O.Ms. No. 111 of 27 June 2005, not 2010; the Lok Sabha passed the Bill on 11 July 2014; it was AP's area that rose to 1,62,970 sq km.

st.1: Visakhapatnam and Kakinada are the major ports.
st.3: Vodarevu and Nizampatnam are being developed on the BOST model.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: Krishnapatnam, a PPP BOST port, was India's largest private port at commissioning. Visakhapatnam is the only major port (Kakinada is non-major); Vodarevu and Nizampatnam are BOOT projects; the Act asks the Union to examine a major port at Duggirajupatnam, not Machilipatnam.

st.1: Its installed capacity includes thermal, hydel, gas and renewable power, with no nuclear share.

x: All three statements are correct: AP's mix is thermal, hydel, gas and renewable with no nuclear; solar is the largest renewable; NTPC Simhadri is 2,000 MW.

st.2: Visakhapatnam's proposed beach-shack policy is modelled on Goa.

x: All three statements are correct: Rushikonda has Blue Flag status; Vizag's beach-shack policy follows Goa; Gandikota is one of the seven anchor hubs.

st.1: CBLO, introduced on 20 January 2003, was a money market instrument operated by the CCIL.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: CBLO (January 2003) was a CCIL money market instrument, now replaced by TREPS. Statement 3 is not: on the Vaghul Committee's advice Certificates of Deposit came in 1989 and Commercial Paper in 1990, not the other way round.

st.1: Asteroids are made mainly of ice and dust.

x: Neither statement is correct: asteroids are mainly rock and metal (ice and dust make comets); comets move in more eccentric, highly elliptical orbits than asteroids.

st.1: It is an apparent force caused by the Earth's rotation.

x: All three statements are correct: the Coriolis force arises from the Earth's rotation, deflects to the right in the north and left in the south, and is zero at the Equator and maximum at the poles.

st.3: The rotation of the Earth causes day and night, not the seasons.

x: All three statements are correct: seasons come from revolution combined with the axial tilt (66½° to the orbital plane), while rotation causes day and night.

st.1: Compositional layering of the Earth consists of the lithosphere, asthenosphere and mesosphere.

x: Neither statement is correct: compositional layering is crust, mantle and core, while lithosphere, asthenosphere and mesosphere (with the outer and inner core) form the mechanical layering, which is not just crust, mantle and core.

st.1: It is most likely on gentle slopes of less than about 10 degrees.
st.4: The Deccan plateau and the Thar are the regions most at risk.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: in India the main trigger is south-west monsoon rain, then earthquakes. Mass wasting is likeliest on slopes above about 30 degrees; creep is very slow (the fast water-soil-rock flow is a mudflow); the Himalaya and the North-East are most at risk.

st.1: Wind is the main agent of coastal erosion.

x: Neither statement is correct: waves, not wind, are the main agent of coastal erosion; saltation is a wind process, not one of the coastal erosion processes.

st.3: The Gobi lies in the Tarim basin of Xinjiang.
st.4: The Thar is the most sparsely populated desert.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the Atacama is the driest place on Earth. Las Vegas lies in the Mojave, not the Sonoran; the Tarim basin holds the Taklamakan, not the Gobi; the Thar is the most densely populated desert.

st.4: Conduction heats the upper layers of air that are far from the warm ground.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: advection is horizontal heat transfer (the Loo) and terrestrial radiation is long-wave. The atmosphere is heated mainly by terrestrial long-wave radiation, not incoming short-wave; conduction heats the lower layers in contact with the ground.

st.3: The latent heat that powers thunderstorms and cyclones is released during condensation.

x: All three statements are correct: the latent heat of fusion is about 80 cal/g and of vaporisation about 540 cal/g; storms are powered by latent heat released on condensation.

st.3: Ground-level ozone, unlike stratospheric ozone, harms living organisms rather than shielding them from UV-B.

x: All three statements are correct: ground-level ozone is a secondary pollutant from NOx and VOCs, rises in heatwaves over the north-west and the Indo-Gangetic Plain, and is harmful, unlike the protective stratospheric ozone.

st.1: In the three-layer system, the thermocline is the warm top layer, about 500 m thick.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct: the deep layer is about 0–4°C and NIOT's Nellore station runs OMNI buoys. The thermocline is the middle layer at about 500–1,000 m, below the warm surface layer; the sea is blue because of scattering, not interference.

st.2: It turns south at Namcha Barwa and enters India through the Shipki La gorge.
st.4: The Dihang becomes the Brahmaputra after the Teesta joins it near Sadiya.
st.1: It rises at the Chemayungdung glacier, west of Mansarovar.

x: None of the statements is correct: the Brahmaputra rises east, not west, of Mansarovar; it enters India through the Dihang gorge (Shipki La is the Sutlej's entry); only about 885 km of its 2,900 km lies in India; it becomes the Brahmaputra after the Dibang and Lohit join near Sadiya, the Teesta joining in Bangladesh.

st.1: It rises at Talakaveri in Wayanad and meets the Bay of Bengal near Poompuhar.
st.2: The Kabini joins it at Srirangapatna.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: the KRS and Mettur dams are on the Kaveri. It rises at Talakaveri in Kodagu, not Wayanad; the Kabini joins at Tirumakudalu Narsipur; the Hemavathi is a left-bank tributary.

st.4: The Kalyani dam is in YSR Kadapa district.
